items.description:
Whether a backup is configured for this resource, and if not why not. One of the
independent axes of resource status, alongside `complianceStatus` — neither
outranks the other, and a pending customer action is reported as a blocker rather
than as a status here.
In scope, and counted:
`INITIAL_CLASSIFICATION` — found, type still being worked out.
`ACCESS_LOST` — Eon can no longer reach the resource; permissions were removed or
changed, and nobody decided this.
`CLASSIFICATION_FAILED` — Eon tried repeatedly to classify it and gave up. The
type is supported; something about this instance defeated it.
`UNASSIGNED` — classified and eligible, but no backup policy covers it.
`ASSIGNED` — a backup policy covers it, storage-gateway policies included: this
axis answers whether a backup is configured, not who takes it.
Out of scope, and not counted — four causes with one shared consequence, kept
distinct because a customer can do different things about each:
`TERMINATED` — deleted in the cloud.
`DISCONNECTED` — the customer told Eon not to discover it, by deactivating the
account or by a discovery exclusion rule.
`EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP` — the customer chose not to back it up.
`UNSUPPORTED` — Eon cannot back up this kind of resource.

configurationStatus.description: Filters for whether a backup is configured for the resource.

items.description:
Whether the resource meets the controls applied to it. Independent of
`configurationStatus` — it is evaluated whether or not a backup policy is assigned,
since a resource with no policy can already violate a control that says it must
be backed up.
`COMPLIANT` — no violations. This is the default: a resource no control applies
to reads compliant rather than "not evaluated".
`VIOLATIONS` — at least one open violation.
`ALL_MUTED` — the resource has violations and every one of them is muted.
There is deliberately no value for "nothing to check". Derived from the
resource's issues on each request rather than stored, so it cannot drift out of
step with `controlViolationCounts`. Absent only when the resource's issues could
not be read for the response.

query.description:
Free-text query for drive, shared-drive and Team searches; it matches item paths and names.
Required by those searches, and ignored by the mail search, which is driven by emailSearchFilter.

to.description: Recipient email addresses or partial matches (OR within)

Optional, but must be sent together with endTime. Restricts to items
captured on or after this time; filtering is at day granularity.

endTime.description:
Optional, but must be sent together with startTime. Restricts to items
captured on or before this time; filtering is at day granularity.

tools.name: restore_microsoft365_user_mail_by_entity
tools.description:
Description: Restores a selected message of one Microsoft 365 user from an Eon snapshot
back into that same user's mailbox, addressing the user by its Eon
saasEntityId. Messages are always imported as new messages into a
destination folder; existing mail is never overwritten.

The restore runs on compute in the Azure restore subscription linked to
the selected Microsoft 365 restore account.

This operation is asynchronous. It triggers a restore job and returns the
job ID, which can be used to track the progress of the restore job via
Get Restore Job.

projectId.description: ID of the project the snapshot is in.

id.description: Eon-assigned resource ID of the Microsoft 365 tenant.

saasEntityId.description: Eon id of the entity to restore.

snapshotId.description: ID of the Eon snapshot to restore from.

X-Action-Approval-Request-Id.description:
ID of an approved action request.
Applicable only when the method is protected by an action approval policy and the action request has been approved. 


When used, the current API request must match the original request parameters.
The approved action request can be executed only by the original requester.

restoreAccountId.description:
The Microsoft 365 restore account to run the restore in. It supplies the
restore-workspace tenant and is linked to the Azure restore subscription
that hosts the restore compute.

restoreScope.description:
What the restore covers. Only the selected message (`SELECTED_ITEMS`) can
be restored; its options live in `selectedItems`.

items.description:
The message to restore, as the opaque itemId returned by
searchSaasUserMail. Exactly one message per restore. The message is
imported back into the user's own mailbox as a new message.

folderName.description:
Name of the mail folder the message is imported into. When empty, the
server generates a default of the form `Eon Restore <timestamp>`.

selectedItems.description: Options for the selected-message restore. Used only when `restoreScope` is `SELECTED_ITEMS`.

targetSaasEntityId.description:
The `saasEntityId` of another live user to restore the selected message into, instead of its
owner. Allowed only when the source user is terminated; the target must have a mailbox. The
message is imported into `selectedItems.folderName` in the target's mailbox.

tools.name: restore_microsoft365_user_drive_by_entity
tools.description:
Description: Restores selected files and folders of one Microsoft 365 user's OneDrive
from an Eon snapshot back into that same OneDrive, addressing the user by
its Eon saasEntityId. Items land either at their original path (overwrite
mode) or under a destination folder.

The restore runs on compute in the Azure restore subscription linked to
the selected Microsoft 365 restore account.

This operation is asynchronous. It triggers a restore job and returns the
job ID, which can be used to track the progress of the restore job via
Get Restore Job.

projectId.description: ID of the project the snapshot is in.

id.description: Eon-assigned resource ID of the Microsoft 365 tenant.

saasEntityId.description: Eon id of the entity to restore.

snapshotId.description: ID of the Eon snapshot to restore from.

X-Action-Approval-Request-Id.description:
ID of an approved action request.
Applicable only when the method is protected by an action approval policy and the action request has been approved. 


When used, the current API request must match the original request parameters.
The approved action request can be executed only by the original requester.

restoreAccountId.description:
The Microsoft 365 restore account to run the restore in. It supplies the
restore-workspace tenant and is linked to the Azure restore subscription
that hosts the restore compute.

restoreScope.description:
What the restore covers. Only the selected items (`SELECTED_ITEMS`) can be
restored; their options live in `selectedItems`.

itemId.description:
Opaque Eon item id from a SaaS search result, passed back verbatim. The
gateway resolves it to the stored item; it is never built or parsed by the
caller.

isDirectory.description:
Whether the item is a folder. When true, Eon restores the whole subtree
under it; when false or omitted, only the single item.

items.description:
OneDrive items to restore, as the opaque itemIds returned by
searchSaasUserDrive, belonging to one user. They are restored back into
that user's own OneDrive. A folder (isDirectory=true) restores its full
nested subfolder hierarchy, nested under the selected folder's own name,
and only with `COPY_TO_NEW_FOLDER`. Empty subfolders are not recreated.

restoreMode.description:
How the restore resolves the destination. `OVERWRITE` replaces files
only, so a selection that includes a folder must use
`COPY_TO_NEW_FOLDER`.

folderName.description:
`COPY_TO_NEW_FOLDER` only: name of the destination folder. When empty, the
server generates a default of the form `Eon Restore <timestamp>`.

selectedItems.description: Options for the selected-items restore. Used only when `restoreScope` is `SELECTED_ITEMS`.

targetSaasEntityId.description:
The `saasEntityId` of another live user to restore the selected items into, instead of their
owner. Allowed only when the source user is terminated; the target must have a OneDrive. The
items are written into `selectedItems.folderName` in the target's OneDrive, so
`selectedItems.restoreMode` must be `COPY_TO_NEW_FOLDER`.

already has the name, including one deleted recently, the restore uses
the next free name with a `(restored <date>)` suffix.

tools.name: restore_microsoft365_user_by_entity
tools.description:
Description: Restores a Microsoft 365 user's per-app data from an Eon snapshot, back to
that same user, addressing the user by its Eon saasEntityId. OneDrive items
always overwrite existing destination items; mailbox messages are always
imported as new messages in a dedicated destination folder, so there is no
destination to choose. Include a workload under `workloads` to restore it;
omit it to skip.

A failure on one workload does not abort the other, and any failed workload
fails the job.

The restore runs on compute in the Azure restore subscription linked to
the selected Microsoft 365 restore account.

This operation is asynchronous. It triggers a restore job and returns the
job ID, which can be used to track the progress of the restore job via
Get Restore Job.

projectId.description: ID of the project the snapshot is in.

id.description: Eon-assigned resource ID of the Microsoft 365 tenant.

saasEntityId.description: Eon id of the entity to restore.

snapshotId.description: ID of the Eon snapshot to restore from.

X-Action-Approval-Request-Id.description:
ID of an approved action request.
Applicable only when the method is protected by an action approval policy and the action request has been approved. 


When used, the current API request must match the original request parameters.
The approved action request can be executed only by the original requester.

restoreAccountId.description:
The Microsoft 365 restore account to run the restore in. It supplies the
restore-workspace tenant and is linked to the Azure restore subscription
that hosts the restore compute.

type.description:
Which app a Microsoft 365 whole-user restore entry covers.
- `MAILBOX`: the user's whole mailbox, imported back into their own mailbox
  as new messages in a dedicated destination folder.
- `ONEDRIVE`: the user's whole OneDrive, restored in place into their own
  OneDrive, overwriting existing items at their original paths.

items.description:
One app to restore for the user, tagged by `type`. No options today; an entry is
just its `type`. Each app restores into the user's own mailbox or OneDrive.

workloads.description:
The apps to restore for the user, one entry per app. Each entry is tagged by
`type`. At least one entry is required.

targetSaasEntityId.description:
The `saasEntityId` of another live user to restore the selected workloads into, instead of the
user itself. Allowed only when the source user is terminated; the target must have every
selected workload. The data is written into a new folder named after the source user, in the
target's OneDrive and mailbox, and nothing existing is overwritten.

tools.description:
Description: Takes an on-demand snapshot of the specified resource.

This operation is asynchronous.
It triggers a backup job and returns a job ID, which can be used to track the progress of the backup job.
You can follow the progress of the backup job by calling Get Backup Job with the job ID.

projectId.description:
ID of the project the resource is in.
You can get your project ID from the API Credentials page in your global management console.

id.description: Eon-assigned ID of the resource to back up.

vaultId.description: Eon-assigned ID of the vault to store the snapshot in.

retentionDays.description: Number of days to retain the snapshot.

isPitrOnDemand.description: Indicates if the snapshot is an on-demand PITR (Point-In-Time Recovery) snapshot for SAP HANA databases.

vaultStorageTier.description: Storage tier used for this snapshot's data. Defaults to standard when omitted.

tools.name: create_action_approval_request
tools.description:
Description: Submit or discard an action request that's in its initial `CREATED` status.

When submitting, the action request status changes to pending approval.
The approval window begins, and reviewers must approve before the window ends.

When discarding, the action request is abandoned, and no further action can be taken.

projectId.description: ID of the project.

action.description:
Action to take on the initial request.
The requester can submit (confirm) or discard the request.

comment.description: Comment from the requester explaining why they want to perform the action.
